provenance.who: a coding-agent session (the one that owns the publisher), from the code and docs of the publisher and from content-blind measurements of its sheet on a mock Canvas in headless Chromium at 390x844 touch (python3 -m speedkit.rehearse); nobody has used this flow on a phone
provenance.note: speeds-kit commit ab19308f5d7fe98f886d10839d73a154dc04fd97 (draft publisher 0.3.1), the file the owner holds: sha256 bcd2947ae99891fe21b2a7f508e24f30158692a14522297a9b1719711770b621 (reproducible from that commit's template and the data). Written BEFORE the owner's first run, so this file is a prediction and not a record. It replaces the fixture of the registration for 0.2.2 (drunken-emu 3e87f6f), which was for a build without the audit layer (A1-A4), at B = 3, and asked the owner for narration and screenshots, which the owner's rule 2 forbids. B = 2 is the primary budget; inside the sheet the goal, the numbers and the written student's name are shown by the sheet (the dock's button, the file line and the foot, the note), so they are not held: that is a hypothesis, and the registration says what would falsify it. The save-from-chat steps reuse the properties the owner STATED about HW1 (tapgrade_0_6_7_sample_pass.json, steps 2-7). Steps marked [guess] are not from anything the owner said; steps marked [declared] are judgments about what the screen says, made by the author of the publisher (P-02be: silence means nothing was declared wrong); [measured] is a number of docs/predictions/draft-publish-first-run.measured.json. The two Canvas-only chains (dp-manual-set, dp-manual-post) are the Gradebook routes the publisher's doc offers; they are written from the author's knowledge of Canvas, not from this owner.
